source.note: Photos and captions from kadiak.org (Kodiak Military History Museum site). Captions in [brackets] are short descriptions added by Kodiak Maps where the page has none.

first_team.caption: First satellite tracking team, September 1959. Back row: Don Jacob, Dale Thompson, Dixie McGehee, Joe Weitzell, Bobby Smith, Jim Warren, Marion Reed, Jim Swarthout. First row: Floyd (Smitty) Smith, Dick Sewell, Frank Lopez, Bob Martin, Stan Shoup, Hank Ciano, Stan Frisby, Jerry Brookman. Kneeling: Bill Emerson, Cliff Spencer, Lee Louffbrow, Bob Grilli, Lou Espinoza, Gene Banks, Reuben Dominquez, Bill farley.
first_team.credit: Image courtesy of Bob Grill, Houston Texas, 2015 May (via kadiak.org)

track2.caption: 2 - Main building on the left, graveyard shift bunks with prelort radar behind. The prelort antenna dome was rigid. (2000 note: The antenna may survive behind the Chiniak post office and the dome at the Gibson Cove highway shop.)

track3.caption: 3 - View from T hill back toward main facility. The lake on the left was the source of drinking water.

track4.caption: 4 - Helix antenna mount and day crew bunks. The dome for the helix antenna was inflated. Bob Hornel kept it blown up.

track5.caption: 5 - Substation, water tanks, helix antenna mount "C".

track6.caption: 6 - This garage building was built as the facility was being closed. It was never used by the Air Force but was used during 1998 as the headquarters for a logging operation. The supply building is just visible on the left along with a corner of the main building.

track7.caption: 7 - Bore sight tower. Aluminum scaffolding with stairs. This tower was used with surveying instruments to align antennas.

track8.caption: 8 - Composite building. Roof area with vents is the chow hall, just beyond is a blank flat roof over the secure area. Beyond that are the eight muffler exhaust stacks of the main power plant generators. On the right is the Prelort tower with missing antenna.

secure1998.caption: 10 - 1998 photo of telephone equipment in the secure area. The roof has been gone for several years.

track11.caption: 11 - Bore-sight tower and housing trailers from antenna "D". Microwave dish was Lenkurt 74 radio to Pillar Mt. Lenkurt 45 mux was used.

track12.caption: 12 - Close-up of bore-sight tower with helix antenna.

track13.caption: 13 - Generator room showing 8 exhaust pipes and fiberglass radome.

track15.caption: 15 - USCG 400 MHz relay site. "T" hill portion of AF station. In 1984 this site had a diesel generator running full-time to power the radio relay from Kodiak to Narrow Cape LorSta. In 2000, the tower is still standing but the building is gone. The tower was removed sometime around 2002.
